purpose: Represent the Cuban Friendship Urn's contemporaneous inscriptions as web-accessed object evidence, distinct from the later National Register narrative that transcribes them.
evidence_decision: The physical inscription is the primary evidentiary object. The NPS National Register nomination is used as the web retrieval/transcription witness, not treated as the origin of the inscription's claim. The material-provenance inscription directly supports reuse of a marble column fragment from the Havana Maine Monument. The Machado inscription only corroborates presentation by Machado and does not prove financing, private contributors, sculptor, or the mechanics of delivery.

value.title: Cuban Friendship Urn contemporaneous inscriptions — material provenance and Machado presentation text
value.publisher_or_creator: Inscription on Cuban Friendship Urn; web transcription/documentation via National Park Service National Register nomination
value.authority_scope: Contemporaneous text physically attached to the object concerning the marble source monument and Gerardo Machado presentation/friendship wording
value.independence_note: The inscription is primary object evidence for what the object itself records. The NPS nomination is the transcription/retrieval witness and must not be counted as a second independent root for the same inscription text.
value.credibility_note: High authority for the inscription's own wording and for the physical material-provenance statement memorialized on the object. More limited for reconstructing the full presentation event or identifying financing, authorship, or contributors.

value.locator: base inscription transcribed/described in National Register nomination, Section 7 page 2
value.evidence_note: The urn's base inscription states that the urn was sculpted from a fragment of the marble column of the Monument to the Victims of the Maine in Havana and identifies the 20 October 1926 hurricane as the event that toppled the column.
value.inheritance_note: The claim is recorded on the object itself. The NPS nomination supplies web access and transcription but is not the upstream origin of the inscription claim.

value.locator: front inscription/plaque described in National Register nomination, Section 7 page 2
value.evidence_note: The object's inscription is attributed to Gerardo Machado and records the Cuba–United States friendship/presentation context. It corroborates Machado's role but does not by itself reconstruct the mechanics of the January 1928 presentation event.
value.inheritance_note: The inscription is contemporaneous object evidence. Its commemorative wording is treated more cautiously than the material-provenance inscription for event reconstruction.
